rounds.text: Gandhar Oil Refinery is currently trading at a significant valuation discount, with a P/E ratio of 5.39x [E1] that sits well below the sector benchmark of 14.21x [E6]. This undervaluation is underscored by a robust intrinsic value estimate of Rs 806 per share, providing a substantial margin of safety of 68.9% [E41, E42]. The company’s operational efficiency is exceptional, evidenced by an ROCE of 33.8% [E10] and an ROE of 25.91% [E9], both of which vastly outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the firm has demonstrated aggressive growth, with trailing twelve-month sales growth of 48% [E17] and profit growth of 388% [E21], supported by a successful capacity expansion to 838,637 kiloliters [E77]. Institutional confidence is rising, as evidenced by positive money flow and an increase in foreign institutional holdings from 2.53% to 5.46% [E38, E40]. Conceded: the company has experienced inconsistent operating margins over the last three years [E28] and a decline in domestic institutional holdings [E39]. Despite these challenges, the company maintains a conservative financial profile with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.14x [E33] and a comfortable current ratio of 2.61x [E34].

The business exhibits severe historical volatility and structural deceleration in its multi-year metrics, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of -11% over the last three years [E20] and a meager 1% compounded sales growth over the same period [E16]. This is accompanied by a low return on equity of 10.3% over the last 3 years [E57] and an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend [E28]. Furthermore, domestic institutional holdings have experienced a sharp contraction, dropping by 5.54 percentage points from 6.61% in December 2023 to 1.07% as of September 2026 [E39], signalling a retreat by sophisticated domestic capital. The company's historical risk profile is underscored by a steep worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -61.9% [E49] and a weak Sharpe ratio of 0.17 [E51], while ongoing operations face acute external headwinds including base oil price uncertainty, West Asian tensions, and volatile shipping routes that disrupt supply chains [E89, E90]. Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 5.39 against a sector benchmark of 14.21x [E1, E6], exhibits strong recent TTM sales and profit growth [E17, E21], and maintains a healthy balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.14x [E33].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over the last 3 years is -11% [E20] and compounded sales growth is 1% [E16]. However, focusing purely on a static 3-year window ignores the explosive inflection occurring right now, highlighted by trailing twelve-month profit growth of 388% [E21] and sales growth of 48% [E17]. Conceded: the yearly operating-margin trend reads inconsistent [E28] and the 3-year average ROE is a modest 10.3% [E57]. Yet, the business has dramatically accelerated profitability into the present, with quarterly operating margins surging to 16% against 6% a year ago (+10 percentage points) [E27]. The retreat in domestic institutional holdings [E39] is entirely offset by surging foreign institutional interest, which expanded by 2.93 percentage points to 5.46% [E38], driving a net POSITIVE MONEY FLOW of +4.24 percentage points [E40]. While the historical drawdown [E49] and weak Sharpe ratio [E51] capture past cyclicality, management has fortified the balance sheet by reducing total borrowings down to Rs 233 Cr [E35] and achieving a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.14x [E33], entirely muting the operational friction of external shipping challenges [E89, E90].

The bull’s reliance on trailing twelve-month growth figures [E17, E21] ignores the reality that these metrics are highly volatile and inconsistent, as evidenced by the -11% compounded profit growth over the last three years [E20] and the 1% sales growth over the same period [E16]. Conceded: the company has improved its quarterly operating margin [E27] and reduced debt [E35, E87]. However, this recent performance is explicitly described as "cyclical" [E54], and management itself warns that the operating environment remains challenging due to unpredictable base oil prices and global shipping disruptions [E89, E90]. While the bull highlights foreign institutional inflows [E38], it glosses over the significant exit of domestic institutions, who reduced their stake by 5.54 percentage points [E39]. Furthermore, the company’s historical performance is marred by a -61.9% peak-to-trough drawdown [E49] and a poor Sharpe ratio of 0.17 [E51], suggesting that the current valuation may not adequately price in the risk of future volatility. Finally, the reliance on a single quarter's margin expansion [E27] contradicts the broader, less impressive 3-year median ROE of 10% [E24, E25] and the "inconsistent" operating-margin trend [E28, E29], indicating that the recent "stellar" performance [E73] may be an outlier rather than a sustainable new baseline.

The bear points to three-year historical deceleration [E16, E20], but ignores the massive inflection in trailing twelve-month performance where sales grew 48% and profit surged 388% [E17, E21]. Conceded: the company experienced a -11% compounded profit growth over 3 years and an inconsistent margin trend [E16, E20, E28, E29], yet the current reality is a dramatic structural upgrade with quarterly operating margins reaching 16% and gross margin spreads hitting INR 29,128 per kl [E27, E81]. While domestic institutions trimmed holdings [E39], foreign institutions concurrently increased their stake by 2.93 percentage points, driving a POSITIVE MONEY FLOW signal [E38, E40]. The bear worries about historical drawdowns and a low Sharpe ratio [E49, E51], but dismisses the exceptional return profile where ROCE reaches 33.8% and ROE hits 25.91% against sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Finally, management does not treat this performance merely as a temporary blip, explicitly anticipating that margins will continue at stellar levels for the next one or two quarters while capacity utilization sits firmly at 82% [E73, E85].

The bull’s reliance on trailing twelve-month growth [E17, E21] ignores the reality that this performance follows a three-year period of stagnant sales growth at 1% and negative profit growth of -11% [E16, E20]. Conceded: the company has seen a recent surge in margins [E27, E81], yet the evidence explicitly labels the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends as "inconsistent" [E28, E29], suggesting these "stellar" levels may be transient rather than a structural shift. While the bull highlights foreign institutional interest [E38], it glosses over the significant exit of domestic institutions, who reduced their holdings by 5.54 percentage points [E39]. The bull cites high ROCE and ROE [E9, E10], but these figures contradict the company's own filed statements, which report a more modest 13.3% ROCE and 10.5% ROE [E12, E13]. Furthermore, the bull’s optimism regarding future margins [E73] is directly countered by management’s own warnings that the operating environment remains challenging due to geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, and uncertain raw material prices [E89, E90]. Finally, the bull ignores that the company’s historical volatility is marked by a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -61.9% and a low Sharpe ratio of 0.17, indicating that the current price appreciation carries significant risk [E49, E51].

As the installed capacity remains unchanged of Texol of 2,35,924, the total installed capacity now stands at 838,000 which is an enhancement of 240,000 over the existing capacity of 5,98,000, which is basically on account of the capitalization over the last few quarters of the capital WIP.
